column1: # names.tsv: the commands, settings, removed settings and hook paths of swarm-dev v0.31.3, frozen
# for the Go port. tests/port_names_test.sh fails on each one that is gone, naming this file and it.
# Rows are tab-separated: kind, name, where. Line numbers in the where column are as of v0.31.3.
# v0.31.2 has the same names. Between the two tags, bin/swarm.sh changes one usage comment line
# (dropped-lines took --story) and hooks/hooks.json does not change.
# The kinds, and what the test checks for each:
#   command: still an arm of bin/swarm.sh's dispatch, or of the early case that runs before it, read
#     as tests/doc_check_test.sh reads them. 68 rows: 66 dispatch arms, 18 of them internal `_` arms,
#     plus version and update. When binary-wrapper moves a ported command's arm out of dispatch, the
#     test must read that command's marker file too.
#   setting: a key of CONFIG_KEYS. 25 rows. `swarm.sh config` in a stand-in project prints a
#   removed-setting: a key a config may still set. 5 rows. A config that sets it still loads. When the
#     where column starts with REMOVED_KEYS, stderr also has a warning naming the key. lessons_file
#   hook: 11 rows. Ten are `<event> <command>`: hooks/hooks.json still runs that command on that event,
#     and the script exists. The eleventh is bin/gh-shim/gh, which no event runs: swarm.sh puts it
#     first on PATH. The test checks that it exists and can be run.
